plumbing.review:
1. **[P2] Fallback can erase previously saved activity.** [finished_activity.go:45](repo/internal/dashboard/finished_activity.go:45) rebuilds the entire transcript against the workspace’s current contents. If fallback deletes or renames a previously read file, the existing path checks reject that earlier event, and the replacement snapshot loses its verified path, read count and size. The fallback test keeps both files present ([finished_activity_accept_test.go:264](repo/cmd/invariant/finished_activity_accept_test.go:264)), so it misses this case. Preserve already-sanitized activity across attempts and add deletion/rename coverage.

2. **[P2] Valid large events prevent snapshot creation.** [finished_activity.go:51](repo/internal/dashboard/finished_activity.go:51) limits events to 32 MiB, while both backend readers accept 64 MiB ([claudecode.go:164](repo/internal/synth/claudecode.go:164), [codex.go:437](repo/internal/synth/codex.go:437)). A valid event between those limits aborts recording before any snapshot is written—or leaves an earlier fallback snapshot stale. Workspace cleanup then makes file activity unrecoverable. Support producer-accepted event sizes and add regression coverage.

Otherwise, the changes stay within scope, the acceptance sources match the plan, and I found no weakened checks, test-specific production behavior, new network access, secret exposure, or material style mismatch. The supplied test report says all checks passed; I did not rerun write-producing tests.

VERDICT: changes needed — preserve verified activity across fallback, handle producer-supported event sizes, and add regression tests for both.
